name: fencing-sterling
label: Sterling — cedar-and-steel fencing one-pager: painted hero ladder, services bento, gallery, process rail, about, reviews, FAQ, estimate CTA
source: Fictional-identity static template (2026-09-02 a-plus rebuild, Lovable lane): the earlier verbatim Sterling Fence port (Bowling Green KY source, retired with the rewrite) was replaced by a hand-authored one-page template whose every identity string is a token. The design language — cedar-green slab hero with grain, ticker, bento services, masonry gallery, numeral process rail, review cards, glass accordion FAQ, estimate CTA panel — is trade-generic; no real business's facts are baked anywhere.
stack: Static A+ build: one hand-authored index.html (real header/main/footer markup, no framework, no CDN, no external requests) + one hand-authored stylesheet at assets/style.css (consuming --wss-* properties throughout; hex literals exist only as the token declarations themselves) + one script asset, assets/index-fencing-sterling.js (the hero video layer: mounts the ladder-marked <video data-hero-video> hidden with no static src and runs the poster-first/tap-to-play control; the hero is complete without it and reduced motion never mounts the clip). Progressive enhancement only — the first inline script adds .js to <html> before first paint, and every sizzle layer (scroll reveals, count-up stats, hero clip arming, magnetic CTA nudge) is inert without JS or under prefers-reduced-motion. The retired Vite/React bundle (assets/index-Z0b1C-j7.js / index-u91_G1Kr.css) is retained UNLOADED as the compiled evidence artifact for the identity scan; the static page never references it. The legacy fence-guides hub (20 static prerendered guides), images/ and sitemap survive from the verbatim port untouched and tokenized.
renders_note: Fixed template copy throughout; it does not consume the engine's content-inject islands (the engine appends its authority block — services, coverage, FAQ, reviews, hours — at the ENGINE INJECTION POINT before the footer, and this one-pager leaves that seam intact). Every business-specific string is a token, and every token that can be unverified collapses its own UI at hydration (see tokens_note). The service set is the vertical's standard six — cedar privacy, ornamental aluminum, vinyl panel, chain link and farm, gates and automation, storm repair — stated as what the trade does, not as claims about a specific contractor.
photo_slots_note: Eight slots, all drawn SVG (no third-party photography rides this template): the hero poster illustration plus six per-slot semantic work illustrations (racked cedar, pool-code aluminum, vinyl side yard, chain-link run, drive gate, braced field corner) and the grain overlay. Each gallery figure's alt text names the KIND of work it depicts — it never claims these drawings are the prospect's own projects.

ladder: the client's own verified clip at client_video_path (engine-placed, mp4, magic-byte verified)
the WSS-owned clip at wss_fallback_clip_path (ships in this donor)
the painted hero surface (the head's data-wss-hero-fallback block paints the family slab colour under the marked video, and the hero-visual poster img stands beside it — the complete zero-JS hero)
the drawn hero composition (slab, grain and scrim layers under everything)
hero_video.note: The shipped fallback bytes are the fencing clip carried over from the verbatim port (no people, no third-party marks). The marked <video data-hero-video muted loop playsinline preload=none hidden> is MOUNTED by the hero layer bundle (assets/index-fencing-sterling.js, the ladder-donor mount contract: hidden, no static src; this family ships no raster poster, so the CSS surface from the head's data-wss-hero-fallback block is the always-painted rung); the ladder runtime in index.html observes for the mount and arms rungs only when their bytes shipped, reduced motion never mounts or arms the video (guarded in the runtime AND in the mount layer), mobile is surface-first with tap-to-play, and the clip pauses when the hero scrolls away or the tab hides.

hero_floor.why: Final QA Class B (2026-09-04): when the hero clip arms, the words sit on a photograph through the donor scrim, and a light-mode mirror needs a PROVEN veil under them in both modes — the same worst-case hero-wash mathematics, appended as the hero contrast floor without editing the donor bundle.

spa_routes_note: One document; sections are #id anchors (#top, #services, #work, #process, #about, #reviews, #faq, #contact). No client routing of any kind — there is no SPA to declare routes for.
prerendered_note: Fully static — index.html ships the complete page as real header/main/footer markup in source order, so crawlers and no-JS visitors read every word. The 20-page fence-guides hub from the verbatim port ships prerendered HTML per route. JS adds sizzle only (reveals, count-ups, hero clip arming), each gated behind the pre-paint .js class and prefers-reduced-motion.
classification_note: request-estimate: conversion routes through the estimate CTA panel and the tel:/mailto: rails. The header CTA, hero call button, CTA-panel call button, footer phone segment and the floater all collapse entirely when the business has no verified phone, each falling back to a #contact estimate anchor where a primary slot needs a survivor. There is no emergency-call archetype — fence work is planned work.
lead_endpoint_note: No donor-native form. The design converts through tel:/mailto: links and #contact estimate anchors, all token-driven and collapse-guarded. The engine's content-inject lead-capture island (POST /api/quote-request) provides the form path on every mirror, so no stub endpoint could silently swallow leads.
tokens_note: Collapse is [[NEED:TOKEN]] / [[NEED:!TOKEN]] phrase markers around every weld of an OPTIONAL token: blank PHONE removes the header CTA (an estimate anchor takes the slot), the hero call button, the CTA-panel call button, the footer phone segment and the ld+json telephone line, and flips the floater plus the meta/OG sentences to written-estimate copy; blank EMAIL removes the mailto rails; blank LICENSE removes the license chip, the footer license line and the ld+json identifier; blank OWNER_NAME swaps the about sentence to the business-led reading and drops the footer ownership clause and the ld+json founder; blank COUNTY unwelds every county mention from copy, headings and the ld+json areaServed entry; blank POSTAL drops the schema postalCode and the footer ZIP; blank GEO drops the geo.position meta and the footer coordinates; blank PROFILE_URL drops the ld+json sameAs and the footer profile link. Dialable links are href=tel:{{PHONE_DIGITS}} everywhere, so a phone-less build carries no dangling tel: href.
truth_law_removals: The verbatim source business's full NAP (Sterling Fence, Bowling Green KY, (270) 799-3969, Warren County, the satellite-town list and the real owner) left with the verbatim port; the rewrite is a fictional-identity template and no real business's facts are baked anywhere in the shipped bytes.

Template stats on the stat strip (48hr estimate turnaround, 15yr post warranty, 4.9 average rating) are design furniture, not claims — the engine's verified-trust islands override them on real builds, and RATING/REVIEW_COUNT are never invented.

The template's three review cards are fictional demo voices (declared in fabricated_persons); they are placeholder furniture the content-inject reviews island supersedes, and no reviewer content is ever fabricated as a real person's words.
Licensing: the LICENSE token renders only when the prospect's license is verified; every 'Licensed {{LICENSE}}' surface collapses when it is not.
No maps embed, no hours table, no review-carousel widget shipped: coverage/authorities arrive via the engine's own verified islands.
identity_atoms_note: The atoms declared here are the template's own FICTIONAL demo identity (name, NAP, domain, license, profile link from the Lovable builder's fictionalIdentity block). None of it appears in the installed bytes — every identity string is a token — but the scan needs real needles so it can never return clean for arbitrary bytes, and so a future edit that hardcodes any of the demo identity is blocked rather than shipped. donor_city Brookhaven and donor_county Lincoln County are PLACE atoms: a legitimate Brookhaven, MS fencing prospect is excused by the client-place carve-out (scan.js BF-5) because the words on the page are then the client's own verified truth.
notes: A-PLUS REBUILD 2026-09-02 (lovable/fencing-sterling-a-plus): the verbatim SPA page was replaced by the static build described in stack — cedar-green design system on --wss-* properties, painted slab hero with grain and word-by-word display headline, ticker, bento services, masonry SVG gallery, numeral process rail, about with partners strip, review cards, glass accordion FAQ, estimate CTA panel, four-column footer and a single floater. CI-repair pass 2 (fix2/fencing-sterling): restored the WSS manifest schema with the fictional identity atoms so the identity gate can fire; restored vertical 'fencing' (the canonical resolver key) and the alias list; NEED-guarded every OPTIONAL token weld (phone, email, license, owner, county, postal, geo, profile); added the data-wss-hero-fallback kill-switch + paint-under style block, the ladder island and the walker runtime in index.html, and the ladder-donor mount bundle assets/index-fencing-sterling.js; renamed assets/logo-fallback.svg -> mark-fallback.svg (a logo-* filename is a donor brand asset the identity scan must block); restored the realestate-waterline family to its merged main state after the branch carried a stale copy.
